literal: Having thought, having been, even if looked, will be angry of that nature, 'You, who having thought of, you looked?' saying.
translation: Even if I sit and gaze at her with fond memories, her sulking is such that she gets angry, asking, 'Thinking of whom did you look at me?'
modern: நான் அவளது அன்பை நினைத்துக்கொண்டு அவளைப் பார்த்தாலும், 'நீர் வேறு யாரையோ நினைத்துக்கொண்டு என்னைப் பார்த்தீர்' என்று அவள் கோபப்படுவாள்; அவளது ஊடல் அத்தன்மையது.
explanation: The husband describes the extreme sensitivity of his wife's feigned anger (pulavi). Even when he sits quietly and gazes at her, filled with fond memories of their love, she misinterprets his thoughtful look. She immediately gets angry and demands to know which other woman he was thinking about while looking at her. The word 'அனைத்து' (of that nature) highlights how inevitable and delicate her sulking is, finding a reason to quarrel even in his loving gaze.
